subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
subtype: Approach: accepting silently and working nights [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Sunaina, and I sit two desks from Omkar. When the manager asked for the feature by the end of the month, Omkar said "Sure" without opening the estimate sheet. After that Omkar was still at the desk when the cleaners arrived, and at midnight the chat status still glowed green. The testing part was quietly dropped. Two weeks later the release shipped, and by Monday three bugs were live and customers were writing in. At the review the manager said, "Good, so that timeline works. Let's keep this pace next time." Omkar nodded, dark circles under the eyes. I don't know why Omkar said yes without asking. But nobody outside our corner knew what it had cost.

qa.q: How many bugs were live by Monday?
qa.a: Three bugs were live by Monday.

qa.q: What might Omkar have been feeling while nodding at the review?
qa.a: Omkar was probably exhausted and reluctant to admit the strain, judging by the dark circles under the eyes.

qa.q: What could Omkar do before answering the next deadline request, and why?
qa.a: Omkar could check the estimate first and say what fits, because a yes that ignores the numbers hides the real cost from the manager.

qa.q: How might the manager see the result of the release?
qa.a: The manager saw a feature delivered on time and so assumed the timeline was reasonable, without knowing about the late nights and dropped testing.

grounding: Illustrates a junior lead accepting a deadline in silence and working nights, so quality drops and the manager concludes the date was reasonable.
